12 	
13 	## Upgrading
14 	
15 	### Node.js Version
16 	
17 	The minimum Node.js version is now **v18.17**. See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information.
18 	
19 	### Next.js Version
20 	
21 	To update to Next.js version 13, run the following command using your preferred package manager:
22 	
23 	```bash package="pnpm"
24 	pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
25 	```

29 	```

33 	```

36 	bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
37 	```
38 	
39 	### ESLint Version
40

42 	
43 	```bash package="pnpm"

45 	```

49 	```

53 	```

57 	```

60 	
61 	## Next Steps
62 	
63 	After you've updated, see the following sections for next steps:
64 	
65 	- [Upgrade new features](#upgrading-new-features): A guide to help you upgrade to new features such as the improved Image and Link Components.

67 	
68 	## Upgrading New Features
69 	
70 	Next.js 13 introduced the new [App Router](/docs/app) with new features and conventions. The new Router is available in the `app` directory and co-exists with the `pages` directory.
71 	
72 	Upgrading to Next.js 13 does **not** require using the App Router. You can continue using `pages` with new features that work in both directories, such as the updated [Image component](#image-component), [Link component](#link-component), [Script component](#script-component), and [Font optimization](#font-optimization).
73 	
74 	### `<Image/>` Component
75 	
76 	Next.js 12 introduced new improvements to the Image Component with a temporary import: `next/future/image`. These improvements included less client-side JavaScript, easier ways to extend and style images, better accessibility, and native browser lazy loading.
77 	
78 	In version 13, this new behavior is now the default for `next/image`.
79 	
80 	There are two codemods to help you migrate to the new Image Component:
81 	
82 	- [**`next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-to-legacy-image): Safely and automatically renames `next/image` imports to `next/legacy/image`. Existing components will maintain the same behavior.
83 	- [**`next-image-experimental` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-experimental): Dangerously adds inline styles and removes unused props. This will change the behavior of existing components to match the new defaults. To use this codemod, you need to run the `next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod first.

12 	
13 	## Route Handlers
14 	
15 	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
16 	
17 	<Image
18 	  alt="Route.js Special File"
19 	  srcLight="/docs/light/route-special-file.png"
20 	  srcDark="/docs/dark/route-special-file.png"
21 	  width="1600"
22 	  height="444"
23 	/>
24 	
25 	> **Good to know**: Route Handlers are only available inside the `app` directory. They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together.
26 	
27 	### Convention
28 	
29 	Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory:
30 	
31 	```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
32 	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
33 	```
34 	
35 	```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
36 	export async function GET(request) {}
37 	```
38 	
39 	Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`.
40 	
41 	### Supported HTTP Methods
42 	
43 	The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.
44 	
45 	### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs
46 	
47 	In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases.
48 	
49 	### Caching
50 	
51 	Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file.
52 	
53 	```ts filename="app/items/route.ts" switcher
54 	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
55 	
56 	export async function GET() {
57 	  const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
58 	    headers: {
59 	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
60 	      'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
61 	    },
62 	  })
63 	  const data = await res.json()
64 	
65 	  return Response.json({ data })
66 	}
67 	```
68 	
69 	```js filename="app/items/route.js" switcher
70 	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
71 	
72 	export async function GET() {
73 	  const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
74 	    headers: {
75 	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
76 	      'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
77 	    },
78 	  })
79 	  const data = await res.json()
80 	
81 	  return Response.json({ data })
82 	}
83 	```
84 	
85 	> **Good to know**: Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached, even if they are placed alongside a `GET` method that is cached, in the same file.
86 	
87 	#### With Cache Components

12 	
13 	## Route Handlers
14 	
15 	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
16 	
17 	<Image
18 	  alt="Route.js Special File"
19 	  srcLight="/docs/light/route-special-file.png"
20 	  srcDark="/docs/dark/route-special-file.png"
21 	  width="1600"
22 	  height="444"
23 	/>
24 	
25 	> **Good to know**: Route Handlers are only available inside the `app` directory. They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together.
26 	
27 	### Convention
28 	
29 	Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory:
30 	
31 	```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
32 	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
33 	```
34 	
35 	```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
36 	export async function GET(request) {}
37 	```
38 	
39 	Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`.
40 	
41 	### Supported HTTP Methods
42 	
43 	The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.
44 	
45 	### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs
46 	
47 	In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases.
48 	
49 	### Caching
50 	
51 	Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file.

59 	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
60 	      'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
61 	    },
62 	  })
63 	  const data = await res.json()

66 	}
67 	```

14 	
15 	> This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
16 	
17 	Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
18 	
19 	- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
20 	- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
21 	
22 	## `cacheLife`
23 	
24 	[`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
25 	
26 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
27 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
28 	
29 	export async function getProducts() {
30 	  'use cache'
31 	  cacheLife('hours')
32 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	`cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
37 	
38 	| Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
39 	| --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
40 	| `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
41 	| `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
42 	| `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
43 	| `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
44 	| `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
45 	| `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
46 	| `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
47 	
48 	For fine-grained control, pass an object:
49 	
50 	```tsx highlight={2-6}
51 	'use cache'
52 	cacheLife({
53 	  stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
54 	  revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
55 	  expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
56 	})
57 	```
58 	
59 	> **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
60 	
61 	See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
62 	
63 	## `cacheTag`
64 	
65 	[`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
66

69 	
70 	export async function getProducts() {
71 	  'use cache'
72 	  cacheTag('products')
73 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
74 	}
75 	```

79 	
80 	export async function getProducts() {
81 	  'use cache'
82 	  cacheTag('products')
83 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
84 	}
85 	```

1  	---
2  	title: Caching
3  	description: Learn how to cache data and UI in Next.js
4  	related:
5  	  title: Next Steps
6  	  description: Learn more about revalidation and the APIs mentioned on this page.
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/getting-started/revalidating
9  	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
10 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
11 	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
12 	---
13 	
14 	> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
15 	
16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
21 	
22 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
23 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
24 	
25 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
26 	  cacheComponents: true,
27 	}
28 	
29 	export default nextConfig
30 	```
31 	
32 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
33 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
34 	const nextConfig = {
35 	  cacheComponents: true,
36 	}
37 	
38 	module.exports = nextConfig
39 	```
40 	
41 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
42 	
43 	## Usage
44 	
45 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
46 	
47 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
48 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
49 	
50 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
51 	
52 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
53 	
54 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
55 	
56 	### Data-level caching
57 	
58 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:
59 	
60 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
61 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
62 	
63 	export async function getUsers() {
64 	  'use cache'
65 	  cacheLife('hours')
66 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
67 	}
68 	```

16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
21

33 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */

35 	  cacheComponents: true,
36 	}
37

48 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)

18 	
19 	The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
20 	
21 	1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
22 	2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
23 	3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
24 	
25 	With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
26 	
27 	The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
28 	
29 	## Default fields
30 	
31 	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
32 	
33 	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
34 	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
35 	
36 	```html
37 	<meta charset="utf-8" />
38 	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
39 	```
40 	
41 	The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
42 	
43 	## Static metadata
44 	
45 	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
48 	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
49 	
50 	export const metadata: Metadata = {
51 	  title: 'My Blog',
52 	  description: '...',
53 	}
54 	
55 	export default function Layout() {}
56 	```
57 	
58 	```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
59 	export const metadata = {
60 	  title: 'My Blog',
61 	  description: '...',
62 	}
63 	
64 	export default function Layout() {}
65 	```
66 	
67 	You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
68 	
69 	## Generated metadata
70 	
71 	You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
72 	
73 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
74 	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
75 	
76 	type Props = {
77 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
78 	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
79 	}
80 	
81 	export async function generateMetadata(
82 	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
83 	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
84 	): Promise<Met

2  	title: Font Optimization
3  	description: Learn how to optimize fonts in Next.js
4  	related:
5  	  title: API Reference

9  	---
10 	
11 	The [`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) module automatically optimizes your fonts and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.
12 	
13 	It includes **built-in self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no layout shift.
14 	
15 	<AppOnly>
16 	
17 	To start using `next/font`, import it from [`next/font/local`](#local-fonts) or [`next/font/google`](#google-fonts), call it as a function with the appropriate options, and set the `className` of the element you want to apply the font to. For example:
18 	
19 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
20 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
21 	
22 	const geist = Geist({
23 	  subsets: ['latin'],
24 	})
25 	
26 	export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27 	  return (
28 	    <html lang="en" className={geist.className}>
29 	      <body>{children}</body>
30 	    </html>
31 	  )
32 	}
33 	```
34 	
35 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
36 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
37 	
38 	const geist = Geist({
39 	  subsets: ['latin'],
40 	})
41 	
42 	export default function Layout({ children }) {
43 	  return (
44 	    <html className={geist.className}>
45 	      <body>{children}</body>
46 	    </html>
47 	  )
48 	}
49 	```
50 	
51 	Fonts are scoped to the component they're used in. To apply a font to your entire application, add it to the [Root Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout).
52 	
53 	</AppOnly>

56 	
57 	To start using `next/font`, import it from [`next/font/local`](#local-fonts) or [`next/font/google`](#google-fonts), call it as a function with the appropriate options, and set the `className` of the element you want to apply the font to. For example, you can apply fonts globally in your [Custom App](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-app) (`pages/_app`):
58 	
59 	```tsx filename="pages/_app.tsx" highlight={1,4-6,10} switcher

61 	import type { AppProps } from 'next/app'
62

64 	  subsets: ['latin'],
65 	})
66 	
67 	export default function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) {

70 	      <Component {...pageProps} />
71 	    </main>
72 	  )
73 	}
74 	```

95 	
96 	You can automatically self-host any Google Font. Fonts are included as static assets and served from the same domain as your deployment, meaning no requests are sent to Google by the browser when the user visits your site.

99

103	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
104	
105	const geist = Geist({
106	  subsets: ['latin'],

9  	---
10 	
11 	The [`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) module automatically optimizes your fonts and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.
12 	
13 	It includes **built-in self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no layout shift.
14 	
15 	<AppOnly>
16 	
17 	To start using `next/font`, import it from [`next/font/local`](#local-fonts) or [`next/font/google`](#google-fonts), call it as a function with the appropriate options, and set the `className` of the element you want to apply the font to. For example:
18 	
19 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
20 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
21 	
22 	const geist = Geist({
23 	  subsets: ['latin'],
24 	})
25 	
26 	export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27 	  return (
28 	    <html lang="en" className={geist.className}>
29 	      <body>{children}</body>
30 	    </html>
31 	  )
32 	}
33 	```
34 	
35 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
36 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
37 	
38 	const geist = Geist({
39 	  subsets: ['latin'],
40 	})
41 	
42 	export default function Layout({ children }) {
43 	  return (
44 	    <html className={geist.className}>
45 	      <body>{children}</body>
46 	    </html>
47 	  )
48 	}
49 	```
50 	
51 	Fonts are scoped to the component they're used in. To apply a font to your entire application, add it to the [Root Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout).
52 	
53 	</AppOnly>
54 	
55 	<PagesOnly>

For example, you can apply fonts globally in your [Custom App](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-app) (`pages/_app`):

1  	---
2  	title: generateStaticParams
3  	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7  	
8  	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9  	
10 	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11 	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12 	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13 	
14 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18 	
19 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20 	    slug: post.slug,
21 	  }))
22 	}
23 	
24 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26 	export default async function Page({
27 	  params,
28 	}: {
29 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30 	}) {
31 	  const { slug } = await params
32 	  // ...
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40 	
41 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42 	    slug: post.slug,
43 	  }))
44 	}
45 	
46 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48 	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49 	  const { slug } = await params
50 	  // ...
51 	}
52 	```
53 	
54 	> **Good to know**:
55 	>
56 	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57 	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58 	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59 	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60 	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61 	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62 	
63 	## Parameters
64 	
65 	`options.params` (optional)
66 	
67 	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68 	
69 	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70 	
71 	## Returns
72 	
73 	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74 	
75 	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76 	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77 	
78 	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79 	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80 	| `/p

5 	
6 	The Route Segment Config options allow you to configure the behavior of a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) by directly exporting the following variables:

10	| [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams)     | `boolean`                                                         | `true`                     |
11	| [`runtime`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime)                 | `'nodejs' \| 'edge' (deprecated)`                                 | `'nodejs'`                 |
12	| [`preferredRegion`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/preferredRegion) | `'auto' \| 'global' \| 'home' \| string \| string[] (deprecated)` | `'auto'`                   |
13	| [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration)         | `number`                                                          | Set by deployment platform |
14	
15	## Version History
16	
17	| Version      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
18	| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
19	| `v16.0.0`    | `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` removed when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. See [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config). |
20	| `v16.0.0`    | `export const experimental_ppr = true` removed. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-experimental_ppr-route-segment-config-from-app-router-pages-and-layouts) is available.                                                                                                  |
21	| `v15.0.0-RC` | `export const runtime = "experimental-edge"` deprecated. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#transform-app-router-route-segment-config-runtime-value-from-experimental-edge-to-edge) is available.                                                                                 |
</content>

<path>node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md</path>
<content>
1  	---
2  	title: route.js
3  	description: API reference for the route.js special file.
4  	---
5  	
6  	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
7  	
8  	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
9  	export async function GET() {
10 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
11 	}
12 	```
13 	
14 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
15 	export async function GET() {
16 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
17 	}
18 	```
19 	
20 	## Reference
21 	
22 	### HTTP Methods
23 	
24 	A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.
25 	
26 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
27 	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
28 	
29 	export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
30 	
31 	export async function POST(request: Request) {}
32 	
33 	export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
34 	
35 	export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
36 	
37 	export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
38 	
39 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
40 	export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
41 	```
42 	
43 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
44 	export async function GET(request) {}
45 	
46 	export async function HEAD(request) {}
47 	
48 	export async function POST(request) {}
49 	
50 	export async function PUT(request) {}
51 	
52 	export async function DELETE(request) {}
53 	
54 	export async function PATCH(request) {}
55 	
56 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
57 	export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
58 	```
59 	
60 	### Parameters
61 	
62 	#### `request` (optional)
63 	
64 	The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.
65 	
66 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
67 	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
68 	
69 	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
70 	  const url = request.nextUrl
71 	}
72 	```
73 	
74 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
75 	export async function GET(request) {
76 	  const url = request.nextUrl
77 	}
78 	```
79 	
80 	#### `context` (optional)
81 	
82 	- **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.
83 	
84 	```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher
85 	export async function GET(
86 	  request: Request,
87 	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }
88 	) {
89 	  const { team } = await params
90 	}
91 	```
92 	
93 	```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher
94 	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
95 	  const { team } = await params
96 	}
97 	```
98 	
99 	| Example                          | URL            | `params`                           |
100	| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
101	| `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
102	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
103	| `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>

1 	---
2 	title: dynamicParams
3 	description: API reference for the dynamicParams route segment config option.
4 	---
5 	
6 	The `dynamicParams` option allows you to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).
7 	
8 	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
9 	export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
10	```
11	
12	```js filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
13	export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
14	```
15	
16	- **`true`** (default): Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` are generated at request time.
17	- **`false`**: Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` will return a 404.
18	
19	> **Good to know**:
20	>
21	> - This option replaces the `fallback: true | false | blocking` option of `getStaticPaths` in the `pages` directory.
22	> - `dynamicParams` is not available when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
</content>

2  	title: Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)
3  	nav_title: Caching (Previous Model)
4  	description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.
5  	---
6  	
7  	> This guide assumes you are **not** using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) which was introduced in version 16 under the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents).
8  	
9  	## Caching `fetch` requests
10 	
11 	By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
12 	
13 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
14 	export default async function Page() {
15 	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
16 	}
17 	```
18 	
19 	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
20 	export default async function Page() {
21 	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
22 	}
23 	```
24 	
25 	See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
26 	
27 	### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
28 	
29 	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
30 	
31 	```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
32 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
33 	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
34 	
35 	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
36 	  async (id: string) => {
37 	    return db
38 	      .select()
39 	      .from(users)
40 	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
41 	      .then((res) => res[0])
42 	  },
43 	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
44 	  {
45 	    tags: ['user'],
46 	    revalidate: 3600,
47 	  }
48 	)
49 	```
50 	
51 	```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
52 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
53 	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
54 	
55 	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
56 	  async (id) => {
57 	    return db
58 	      .select()
59 	      .from(users)
60 	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
61 	      .then((res) => res[0])
62 	  },
63 	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
64 	  {
65 	    tags: ['user'],
66 	    revalidate: 3600,
67 	  }
68 	)
69 	```
70 	
71 	The third argument accepts:
72 	
73 	- `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
74 	- `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
75 	
76 	See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
77 	
78 	### Route segment config
79 	
80 	You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
81 	
82 	#### `dynamic`
83 	
84 	Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
85 	
86 	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
87 	export const dynamic = 'auto'
88 	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
89 	```
90 	
91 	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
92 	export const dynamic = 'auto'
93 	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
94 	```
95 	
96 	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
97 	- **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
98 	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
99 	  - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
100	- **`'err

6  	The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.

9  	export default function DashboardLayout({

13 	}) {

16 	```
17 	
18 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
19 	export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
20 	  return <section>{children}</section>
21 	}
22 	```
23 	
24 	In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
25 	
26 	A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
27 	
28 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
29 	export default function RootLayout({
30 	  children,
31 	}: {
32 	  children: React.ReactNode
33 	}) {
34 	  return (
35 	    <html lang="en">
36 	      <body>{children}</body>
37 	    </html>
38 	  )
39 	}
40 	```
41 	
42 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
43 	export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
44 	  return (
45 	    <html lang="en">
46 	      <body>{children}</body>
47 	    </html>
48 	  )
49 	}
50 	```
51

53

55 	
56 	#### `children` (required)
57 	
58 	Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
59 	
60 	#### `params` (optional)
61

63

68 	}: {
69 	  children: React.ReactNode

71 	}) {

73 	}
74 	```
75 	
76 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
77 	export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
78 	  const { team } = await params
79 	}
80 	```

events.content:
The Pages Router is fully migrated to the App Router, and the `pages` directory is gone.

- `_app` and `_document` are now the root `app/layout.tsx`, with metadata and `next/font` instead of `next/head` and `next/document`.
- `getServerSideProps`, `getStaticProps`, and `getStaticPaths` are now async server pages, `revalidate`, and `generateStaticParams`.
- `useRouter` comes from `next/navigation`.
- `404` and `_error` are `not-found.tsx`, `error.tsx`, and `global-error.tsx`, using `retry`.
- API routes are typed route handlers. `params` and `headers()` are awaited.

`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx next build` both passed. A local server check confirmed `/`, `/blog`, `/blog/1`, the 404 page, and the posts API.
